mechanism_narrative: The sharp rebound in PARKS mobility signals broader discretionary out-of-home activity returning first in leisure settings, which then spills into retail visits. If PARKS keeps rising from its recent trough, RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks than over the prior four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -37.3 to -6.9 over three weeks while RETAIL_REC improved from -52.7 to -30.7
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to improve but RETAIL_REC is not higher on a 28-day average than in the previous 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT recovers enough to reduce access friction for city-center trips, retail and recreation visits rise within one to two weeks. A further upward move in TRANSIT should therefore lift RETAIL_REC quickly, because shopping trips depend on reachable trip chains.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -40 after being below -45
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -54.9 to -41.7 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses above -40 but RETAIL_REC does not improve within the next 14 days relative to the prior 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL mobility captures more time spent at home, which suppresses retail outings because discretionary trips are postponed. If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated or increases further, RETAIL_REC should remain below its prior four-week average over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remained above baseline at 14.4 to 9.4 while RETAIL_REC stayed deeply negative
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline and RETAIL_REC nevertheless rises above its previous 28-day mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates reopening of commuting and daytime activity networks; together they create more incidental retail opportunities than either series alone. When both rise over the same week, RETAIL_REC should increase over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:Both series improved monotonically in the snapshot while RETAIL_REC also improved
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise together for at least two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC does not increase on a 28-day average, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Retail mobility is most likely to fall again if parks activity surges while workplaces do not recover, because leisure substitution can absorb trips without restoring shopping demand. The trigger is a park-led rebound that outpaces workplace recovery; under that condition RETAIL_REC should decline over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES stays below -20
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rebounded much faster than WORKPLACES in the snapshot
failure_condition: If PARKS jumps by 10 points or more while WORKPLACES remains below -20 and RETAIL_REC still rises over the next 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in GROCERY_PHARM indicates that even essential errand mobility is normalizing back toward routine, which usually precedes broader shopping recovery. If the decline slows and the series stabilizes near its current level, RETAIL_REC should improve within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -21.1 to -9.9 over three weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes near its current level but RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in PARKS combined with lower TRANSIT friction indicates weekend and short-trip leisure activity is replacing constrained commuting, which should support retail footfall after a short lag. This effect should strengthen only when both proxies move in the same direction.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and TRANSIT both improved sharply from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS and TRANSIT both improve but RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES remains suppressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, daytime population dispersion stays weak and retail demand does not recover. In a restriction-tightened regime, that combination should keep RETAIL_REC below its prior four-week mean over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES remained around -24 while RESIDENTIAL stayed positive
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays depressed and RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline but RETAIL_REC rises above its previous 28-day mean, the hypothesis is rejected.
